readers.framing: a maintainer of the library who has to implement this requirement and wants to know exactly what code to write

readings.summary: Add a parameterless GeneratedMessagePackFormatter attribute whose annotated, possibly bodyless partial formatter class receives a generated implementation for T, using public-member contractless serialization by default and honoring any MessagePack attributes already present on T.
readings.code_difference: The generator and any associated declaration-syntax handling need only discover the marker attribute and IMessagePackFormatter<T>, emit Serialize/Deserialize members into that partial class, and inspect T across assembly boundaries; no surrogate-type property or name-based key mapping is implemented.

readings.summary: Implement the formatter-generation feature together with the suggested optional SurrogateType property, using a Project-B-accessible surrogate type to supply property keys and other settings mapped to T's properties by name.
readings.code_difference: In addition to the core generation, the attribute exposes SurrogateType, the generator resolves and validates that type and maps its attributed properties to T by name, and the resulting metadata controls keys/settings instead of relying solely on T's own attributes or contractless defaults.

output.quote: AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.
